title: Parable: Invitation by the Explaining Master and Conduct of the Two Groups

questions.question: In the speech to the people, what does the king want them to learn about him?
questions.answer: He wants them to know who he is and recognize him.

questions.question: How should the people respond when they see the beauty and skill in the palace?
questions.answer: They should value the work, admire it, and try to become beloved to the king.

questions.question: What should the people do because the king shows care for them through his gifts and blessings?
questions.answer: They should love him by obeying him.

questions.question: What response is wanted when the people notice the king’s kindness and mercy in the blessings?
questions.answer: They should thank him and show respect.

questions.question: Why does the king show his perfect beauty through his works?
questions.answer: He wants the people to long to see him and seek his pleasure.

questions.question: What do the special marks on each work show about the king?
questions.answer: They show that everything belongs to him, comes from him, and points to his oneness.

questions.question: After hearing these signs, what truth should the people accept about the king?
questions.answer: They should accept that he is one, unique, and has no equal.

questions.question: After the speech, into how many groups did the people divide?
questions.answer: They divided into two groups.

questions.question: What good qualities did the first group have?
questions.answer: They knew themselves, were smart, and had sound hearts.

questions.question: When the first group looked at the palace, what did they understand about it?
questions.answer: They understood that it had a serious purpose and was not made for nothing.

questions.question: What made the first group want to learn more?
questions.answer: They were amazed by what they saw and wanted to know the secret and meaning behind it.

questions.question: How did the first group realize where the answers could be found?
questions.answer: They heard the teacher speaking and understood that he had the keys to the mysteries.

questions.question: How did the first group speak to the teacher?
questions.answer: They greeted him with peace, honored him, and asked him to explain what the lord had taught him.

questions.question: What did the teacher do for the first group?
questions.answer: He repeated the message to them.

questions.question: How did the first group benefit from listening carefully?
questions.answer: They accepted the message, gained much from it, and acted the way the king wanted.

questions.question: What happened because the king was pleased with the good behavior of the first group?
questions.answer: He invited them to another very special and lofty palace.

questions.question: What kind of reward did the first group receive in the end?
questions.answer: They were given a fitting gift from the king and made happy forever.

questions.question: What was wrong with the second group before they even acted badly?
questions.answer: Their thinking was spoiled and their hearts had become dark.

questions.question: What did the second group pay attention to in the palace?
questions.answer: They only cared about the tasty food.

questions.question: How did the second group treat the teacher’s guidance and the students’ warnings?
questions.answer: They ignored them completely.

questions.question: What animal-like behavior is mentioned about the second group?
questions.answer: They ate greedily and then fell asleep.

questions.question: What mistake did the second group make with the special drinks?
questions.answer: They drank things meant for another purpose.

questions.question: What happened after they became drunk?
questions.answer: They shouted loudly and disturbed the other guests.

questions.question: Why were the second group arrested?
questions.answer: They broke the rules and behaved badly toward the king’s order.

questions.question: What was the final result for the second group?
questions.answer: They were seized by the soldiers and thrown into a prison fit for such rude people.

questions.question: What is the main message of the teacher’s announcement to the people in the palace?
questions.answer: The people should know the king, love him, obey him, thank him, and accept his oneness.

questions.question: Why are the palace decorations important in the teacher’s message?
questions.answer: They help the people see the king’s skill and become closer to him by appreciating his work.

questions.question: What does the king’s giving of blessings show about his feelings toward the people?
questions.answer: It shows love, mercy, and kindness.

questions.question: What should people do when they receive blessings from the king?
questions.answer: They should obey him, respect him, and thank him.

questions.question: What does the king want people to feel when they see the beauty shown in his works?
questions.answer: He wants them to want to see him and seek his favor.

questions.question: What do the unique signs on the works teach about ownership?
questions.answer: They teach that each work belongs to the king alone.

questions.question: What do those same signs teach about the king’s nature?
questions.answer: They show that he is one and has no partner or equal.

questions.question: What happened among the people after the teacher spoke?
questions.answer: They split into two separate groups.

questions.question: Why was the first group able to understand the palace better?
questions.answer: They had self-awareness, intelligence, and good hearts.

questions.question: What conclusion did the first group make when they saw the palace wonders?
questions.answer: They knew there must be a great purpose behind them.

questions.question: What question puzzled the first group before they went to the teacher?
questions.answer: They wondered what secret meaning and hidden key the palace had.

questions.question: What showed the first group that the teacher could explain the mysteries?
questions.answer: His speech made it clear that he understood the palace’s purpose.

questions.question: What was respectful about the first group’s approach to the teacher?
questions.answer: They greeted him politely and asked him humbly to teach them.

questions.question: What two things did the first group do that helped them benefit?
questions.answer: They listened closely and accepted what they heard.

questions.question: What did the first group do after learning the message?
questions.answer: They lived by it and behaved as the king wished.

questions.question: How did the king respond to the first group’s obedience and good manners?
questions.answer: He welcomed them to a higher palace and honored them with lasting happiness.

questions.question: What controlled the second group when they entered the palace?
questions.answer: Their lower desires took control of them.

questions.question: What important things did the second group fail to notice?
questions.answer: They missed the palace’s meanings, the teacher’s guidance, and the warnings.

questions.question: In what way did the second group act without self-control?
questions.answer: They overate, slept carelessly, drank wrongly, and then made a scene.

questions.question: How did the second group affect the other guests?
questions.answer: They bothered and upset them with loud and rude behavior.

questions.question: Why was their behavior not just foolish but also wrong?
questions.answer: It went against the rules of the king who made the palace.

questions.question: What was the ending for people who behaved that way?
questions.answer: They were arrested and put in a prison suited to their bad manners.

questions.question: According to the teacher, why was the palace made and displayed?
questions.answer: It was made so the king could be known through what he showed.

questions.question: What are people expected to do after learning about the king from the palace?
questions.answer: They are expected to recognize him and try to know him better.

questions.question: How can people try to be loved by the king?
questions.answer: By appreciating the beauty and skill in his works.

questions.question: What is one way the king shows love to the people?
questions.answer: He gives them blessings and gifts.

questions.question: What should people do in return for that love?
questions.answer: They should love him by obeying him.

questions.question: What should people offer when they see the king’s mercy and kindness?
questions.answer: They should offer thanks with respect.

questions.question: What does the teacher say about the king’s beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: The king shows them through his works so people will want nearness to him.

questions.question: What is taught by the special marks placed on all the works?
questions.answer: They prove that the works are his alone and point to his uniqueness.

questions.question: What belief about the king should the people accept from all these signs?
questions.answer: They should believe he is one, unmatched, and independent.

questions.question: What separated the people into two different groups?
questions.answer: Their different responses to the palace and the teacher’s message separated them.

questions.question: What made the first group notice that the palace was not a game?
questions.answer: Their clear minds and good hearts helped them see its serious meaning.

questions.question: What did the first group seek after they saw the wonders?
questions.answer: They sought the hidden meaning and key to understanding it all.

questions.question: Why did they go to the teacher instead of guessing by themselves?
questions.answer: They understood that he had the explanation they needed.

questions.question: What did the first group ask the teacher to share with them?
questions.answer: They asked him to tell them what the lord had made known to him.

questions.question: What was the result of the first group’s careful listening?
questions.answer: They benefited greatly and followed the king’s will.

questions.question: What was the long-term result for the first group?
questions.answer: They were given a higher palace and lasting happiness.

questions.question: What inner problem did the second group have?
questions.answer: Their minds were corrupt and their hearts were lifeless.

questions.question: What narrow choice did the second group make when they entered the palace?
questions.answer: They focused only on eating and ignored everything else.

questions.question: How did the second group treat reminders and warnings?
questions.answer: They shut them out and refused to listen.

questions.question: What poor actions led the second group into deeper trouble?
questions.answer: They ate like animals, slept carelessly, drank what was not meant for them, and got drunk.

questions.question: What social harm did the second group cause?
questions.answer: They disturbed the other guests with loud and rude behavior.

questions.question: What does the teacher tell the people the king wants through the palace?
questions.answer: He wants the people to know him through what he has made.

questions.question: What should people do when they see the king’s artistic works?
questions.answer: They should admire them and value them.

questions.question: Besides admiration, what relationship should people try to build with the king?
questions.answer: They should try to become beloved to him.

questions.question: Which action shows love for the king according to the speech?
questions.answer: Obeying him shows love.

questions.question: Which action shows respect for the king because of his gifts?
questions.answer: Thanking him shows respect.

questions.question: What desire should grow in the people when they see the beauty in his works?
questions.answer: They should desire to see him and win his approval.

questions.question: What do the marks and seals on the works say about the maker?
questions.answer: They show that one owner made them all and that he is without equal.

questions.question: After hearing the message, what truth were the people supposed to accept?
questions.answer: They were supposed to accept the king’s oneness and uniqueness.

questions.question: How many kinds of responses to the palace are described after the speech?
questions.answer: Two kinds are described.

questions.question: What does the first group’s self-knowledge tell us about them?
questions.answer: It tells us they were thoughtful and aware of themselves.

questions.question: What did the first group understand about the palace right away?
questions.answer: They understood it had an important purpose.

questions.question: What moved the first group toward the teacher?
questions.answer: Their wonder and questions about the palace’s secret meaning moved them.

questions.question: How did the first group view the teacher?
questions.answer: They saw him as a truthful and precise guide who was needed there.

questions.question: What attitude did the first group have while listening?
questions.answer: They listened with care and openness.

questions.question: What did they do after accepting the teaching?
questions.answer: They lived according to it.

questions.question: What reward matched the first group’s good conduct?
questions.answer: They were invited to a noble new palace and given endless happiness.

questions.question: What was the first sign of the second group’s failure?
questions.answer: They came in with damaged minds and darkened hearts.

questions.question: What did the second group choose instead of understanding?
questions.answer: They chose pleasure and appetite instead of meaning.

questions.question: How is their ignoring of the teacher described?
questions.answer: It is described as shutting themselves off from guidance and warning.

questions.question: What wrong use did they make of what was in the palace?
questions.answer: They used special drinks in a way they were not meant to be used.

questions.question: What happened to their behavior after that?
questions.answer: They became drunk and noisy.

questions.question: How did their conduct relate to the king’s rules?
questions.answer: It broke and disrespected the rules.

questions.question: What was done to them in the end?
questions.answer: The king’s soldiers seized them and put them in prison.

questions.question: In simple words, what was the teacher trying to help the people do?
questions.answer: He was trying to help them understand the king and respond to him the right way.

questions.question: What should people understand from the palace and the things inside it?
questions.answer: They should understand that the king wants to be known.

questions.question: If someone admires the king’s art properly, what should that lead to?
questions.answer: It should lead to becoming loved by the king.

questions.question: What should people do because the king has shown them care through many gifts?
questions.answer: They should obey him and love him in return.

questions.question: What is the right response to the king’s mercy and kindness?
questions.answer: The right response is thankful respect.

questions.question: Why does the teacher mention the king’s perfect beauty?
questions.answer: To show that the people should want closeness to him and seek his pleasure.

questions.question: What do the special signs on every work prove?
questions.answer: They prove the works belong to one king and come from his hand alone.

questions.question: What belief should follow from seeing those signs?
questions.answer: The people should believe the king has no equal or partner.

questions.question: What happened to the crowd after this teaching?
questions.answer: It split into a good group and a bad group.

questions.question: Why was the first group able to think correctly about the palace?
questions.answer: Because they had understanding, self-awareness, and hearts set right.

questions.question: What did they realize about the amazing things in the palace?
questions.answer: They realized those things were meaningful and not pointless.

questions.question: What made them seek out the teacher?
questions.answer: They wanted to know the hidden meaning and understood he could explain it.

questions.question: What did they ask the teacher for?
questions.answer: They asked him to share the message he had received from their lord.

questions.question: What two steps brought benefit to the first group after they met the teacher?
questions.answer: They listened carefully and accepted the teaching.

questions.question: What kind of life did the first group live after that?
questions.answer: They lived in a way that pleased the king.

questions.question: What blessing was given to the first group because of that?
questions.answer: They were welcomed to a higher palace and made happy forever.

questions.question: What ruled the second group when they came into the palace?
questions.answer: Their selfish desires ruled them.

questions.question: What important parts of the palace experience did they miss?
questions.answer: They missed the deeper meanings, the guidance, and the warnings.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the second group lacked discipline?
questions.answer: They ate too much, slept carelessly, and misused the drinks.

questions.question: What happened when they drank what was not meant for them?
questions.answer: They became drunk and acted loudly.

questions.question: Besides harming themselves, whom did they trouble?
questions.answer: They troubled the other guests who were watching.

questions.question: Why did the palace soldiers step in?
questions.answer: Because the group’s rude behavior went against the maker’s rules.

questions.question: What does the prison at the end tell us about wrong choices?
questions.answer: It tells us that bad choices can lead to fitting punishment.

questions.question: What does the teacher say is the king’s purpose in showing the palace to the people?
questions.answer: The king wants to make himself known to them.

questions.question: What should people do after recognizing the king through the palace?
questions.answer: They should try to know him better.

questions.question: How can people answer the king’s wish to be loved?
questions.answer: They can answer it by appreciating his art and admiring his works.

questions.question: What does the king’s giving of blessings show toward the people?
questions.answer: It shows his love for them.

questions.question: What human response is asked for when love is shown in that way?
questions.answer: The people should love him by obeying him.

questions.question: What should people do because the gifts also show mercy and kindness?
questions.answer: They should thank him respectfully.

questions.question: What does the display of perfection and beauty invite people to seek?
questions.answer: It invites them to seek seeing him and gaining his pleasure.

questions.question: What do the special seals on each beautiful work teach about the maker?
questions.answer: They teach that he made them himself and that all belong to him.

questions.question: What final conclusion should people reach about the king from these signs?
questions.answer: They should conclude that he is one, unique, and without any equal.

questions.question: What happened to the people in the palace after the teacher’s message?
questions.answer: They separated into two groups.

questions.question: Which traits helped the first group respond well?
questions.answer: Self-knowledge, intelligence, and upright hearts helped them.

questions.question: What was the first group’s first big realization about the palace?
questions.answer: They realized something very important was happening there.

questions.question: What did the first group want to uncover?
questions.answer: They wanted to uncover the secret meaning behind the palace.

questions.question: Why did they think the teacher was necessary?
questions.answer: They believed a truthful guide was needed to explain such a great place.

questions.question: What happened after the teacher repeated the message to them?
questions.answer: They listened carefully, accepted it, and gained much good from it.

questions.question: What was the first group’s reward for acting as the king wished?
questions.answer: They were invited to a higher palace and given permanent happiness.

questions.question: What kind of inner condition is described for the second group?
questions.answer: They had corrupted minds and darkened hearts.

questions.question: What did the second group choose to focus on?
questions.answer: They focused only on the delicious food.

questions.question: How did they treat the message and warnings around them?
questions.answer: They ignored both the teaching and the warnings.

questions.question: What actions show that the second group acted like animals?
questions.answer: They stuffed themselves with food and then fell asleep.

questions.question: What extra wrong step made their behavior even worse?
questions.answer: They drank special liquids that were meant for another use.

questions.question: What happened after they drank those liquids?
questions.answer: They got drunk and shouted loudly.

questions.question: What two results came from their shouting and rude conduct?
questions.answer: They upset other guests, and then they were arrested and put into prison.
